name: Pomme
shortDescription: Autonomous fruit-picking rover: 5-DOF arm, on-device ripeness detection, lidar SLAM, and a fine-tuned model that turns commands into actions.
description:
Pomme is an autonomous fruit-picking and sorting robot built at Hack the 6ix 2026. A custom rover with a 5-DOF arm drives to fruit, an arm-mounted camera classifies type and ripeness on the robot itself (no cloud), and the fruit lands in the right bin. A 360° lidar builds a live SLAM map, a PlayStation controller handles manual teleop, and everything streams live to [pomme.live](https://pomme.live/).

Under the hood:
- **Arduino UNO Q, split in two:** the Linux MPU runs the camera, on-device vision, arm IK and the pick/sort state machine; the STM32 MCU runs motor PWM, servo interpolation, a sub-10 ms ultrasonic e-stop and a watchdog, so motion never waits on AI.
- **On-device vision:** a locally trained YOLOv8n (ONNX int8) deployed with Edge Impulse, with an OpenCV HSV fallback behind the same detector interface.
- **Lidar SLAM:** RPLIDAR C1 with scan-to-scan ICP odometry and a log-odds occupancy grid, streamed to the dashboard.
- **FarmHand:** a small language model fine-tuned (SFT + GRPO) to turn "pick all the ripe apples" into schema-validated robot actions, asking a clarifying question when a command is ambiguous.
- **Hardware:** 3D-printed 5-DOF arm, differential-drive base, multi-rail power stack.
- **Web:** React + Vite + Three.js dashboard, Express + Socket.IO hub, MongoDB Atlas, Auth0-gated teleop.

Every physical component has a simulated stand-in, so the whole system runs on a laptop.
